parameters.text:
=You are a senior real estate lead qualification analyst. Score the lead below using the EXACT algorithm provided. Be deterministic and consistent — the same input must always produce the same score. Do not improvise weights or invent values.

=========================
LEAD DATA
=========================
Name:           {{ $json.body.name }}
Property Type:  {{ $json.body.propertyType }}
Budget Range:   {{ $json.body.budget }}
Location/City:  {{ $json.body.location }}
Bedrooms:       {{ $json.body.bedrooms }}
Timeline:       {{ $json.body.timeline }}
Message:        {{ $json.body.message }}

=========================
SCORING ALGORITHM
=========================
Compute four component sub-scores (each 0–100), apply the weights, then apply keyword adjustments. Round to the nearest whole number and clamp the final result to 0–100.

1) TIMELINE — weight 40%
   Immediately      = 100
   Within 1 month   = 85
   1-3 months       = 60
   3-6 months       = 35
   Just browsing    = 10
   (blank/unknown)  = 30

2) BUDGET — weight 30%
   Over €1M         = 100
   €500k-€1M        = 85
   €250k-€500k      = 65
   €100k-€250k      = 45
   Under €100k      = 25
   (blank/unknown)  = 30
   NOTE: If Property Type is "Rent", treat the budget tier as monthly rent intent — keep the same point values (higher budget still = stronger lead).

3) COMPLETENESS — weight 20%
   These 7 fields count: Name, Property Type, Budget, Location, Bedrooms, Timeline, Message.
   A field counts as "filled" only if it has a real, non-empty value.
   Score = (number of filled fields / 7) × 100.

4) MESSAGE QUALITY — weight 10%
   Empty / blank                                                = 0
   Generic or one-liner, no specifics (e.g. "interested")       = 40
   Some specifics (a need, a feature, a constraint)             = 70
   Detailed & concrete (clear requirements, motivation, budget  = 100
     confirmation, financing readiness, specific area/property)

BASE SCORE = (Timeline × 0.40) + (Budget × 0.30) + (Completeness × 0.20) + (MessageQuality × 0.10)

KEYWORD ADJUSTMENTS (apply to BASE SCORE, then clamp to 0–100):
   +10 if the Message contains any urgency keyword (case-insensitive):
       "urgent", "immediately", "asap", "quickly"
   -15 if the Message contains any low-intent keyword (case-insensitive):
       "just browsing", "maybe", "not sure"
   Both can apply (net -5). Count each rule at most once regardless of how many matching words appear.

FINAL SCORE = clamp( round(BASE SCORE + adjustments), 0, 100 )

=========================
TIER / LABEL / PRIORITY MAP
=========================
Score 80-100 -> TIER A | LABEL Hot Lead  | PRIORITY Call within 1 hour
Score 60-79  -> TIER B | LABEL Warm Lead | PRIORITY Call today
Score 40-59  -> TIER C | LABEL Cool Lead | PRIORITY Call this week
Score 0-39   -> TIER D | LABEL Cold Lead | PRIORITY Nurture only

=========================
OUTPUT — return EXACTLY this format, nothing before or after, no markdown, no code fences:
=========================
SCORE: [0-100]
TIER: [A/B/C/D]
LABEL: [Hot Lead / Warm Lead / Cool Lead / Cold Lead]
PRIORITY: [Call within 1 hour / Call today / Call this week / Nurture only]
SUMMARY: [exactly 2 sentences written for the agent: who they are, what they want, and why this score]
NEXT_ACTION: [one specific recommended action tailored to this lead — reference their location, property type, timeline, or budget]

How it works / notes

- Weighting is exactly as specified — timeline 40 / budget 30 / completeness 20 / message quality 10, combined into a 0–100 base, then the ±keyword adjustments are applied and clamped.
- Determinism: I gave the model fixed point tables instead of letting it "feel out" a score, so the same lead always yields the same number. For maximum consistency, set the node's temperature to 0 in the model settings.
- Blank handling: unknown timeline/budget default to 30 (mild penalty, not a zero) so a half-filled form doesn't crater unfairly — completeness already penalizes missing fields separately.
- Rent vs Buy: I added a line so rental budgets are read as monthly-rent intent rather than being misjudged against purchase prices. Tell me if you'd rather rentals use a different budget table.
- Output is parser-friendly: strict KEY: value lines, no markdown — easy to split in a downstream n8n Set/Code node (e.g. split on \n, then :).
